about: Claims from Nick's YouTube commentary (September 2026 monthly final and European daily tournaments), paraphrased (never the transcript: public repo). Each claim: approximate match time in seconds (set from the anchor named; the transcripts have no timestamps), kind, the claim, tactics ids, the variable it suggests (comms_vars.py), and the engine's check (agrees, disagrees, partly, can't measure) with the evidence. Vocabulary: SLW = spirit light weapon ritualist; boss = the Boss status of September's flux, Like a Boss (whoever kills the Boss becomes it); it is not the morale boost; Lisa = Avatar of Lyssa dervish; Gren = Grenth's dervish; the auto-transcript often writes 'men' for 'NwAy' or 'SKT'.

d4660b7b-1e09-584e-a786-0e9f48b3f343.teams: Men (Double Paragon WoC spike) against Team (double melee, two mesmers, spirit light weapon ritualist)
d4660b7b-1e09-584e-a786-0e9f48b3f343.alignment: Men archers lost 0:38 and 0:43, Team Mes/A death 0:50, Team split from 1:58, Men boosts 2:55 and 4:55, Team wipe 4:59 to 5:37, Team's first knight 5:45

claims.claim: Double Paragon WoC is a strong 8v8 spike build, a little weak against splits; with Psychic Instability and only Shatter Enchantment for removal, its spikes are obvious and a prot and 8 monk on top of them can stop most.

check.evidence: Team's prot and 8 monk didn't stop them: Team lost 9 players and Men none.

claims.claim: Team's prot lacks Spirit Bond: with only Aura of Faith to stack, one Shatter Enchantment leaves the spike target bare.

check.evidence: Team's Prot died three times (2:18, 3:57, 5:37).

claims.claim: Team splitting from the start shows it read Men as a spike build (or wanted the gate locks with its balance build).

check.evidence: Intent; Team's split formed from 1:58.

claims.claim: Team's early flag run on the mesmer, with the 7 monk at risk, was too eager; meanwhile Team's backside group took Men's outside archers.

check.evidence: Men lost archers at 0:38 and 0:43; Team's Mes/A died at 0:50.

claims.claim: Team's main team played far too aggressively, out in a 3v5 for no reason: a team relying on its split should give up ground, footmen and archers and play in its pit, taking no death penalty and giving no boosts.

check.evidence: Team's deaths came at 4v5 and 3v5 away from the pit (backside 2:18, 4:32); Men boosted at 2:55 and 4:55.

claims.claim: Team's split took the 8 monk, the spirit light weapon and the mesmer, leaving its main badly underpowered against Men's whole spike team.

check.evidence: Team's main lost 7 players from 2:18 to 5:37 while the split took one knight (5:45).

claims.claim: Holding the flag to tie up the enemy prot only helps if the advantage is used somewhere else; otherwise it just lets the enemy keep its damage together.

check.evidence: Team held its flag until 5:17 (262 s after Men's capture) and gained nothing at main.

claims.claim: Team's split finally took a knight, but nothing else, and Team's Lord was nearly dead.

check.evidence: Men lost a knight at 5:45; Men won at 6:13.

457b3a21-b67f-5164-a70d-adfd73423fcf.result: SKT won at 28:00 on Lord damage, by a fraction of a second (Nick)
457b3a21-b67f-5164-a70d-adfd73423fcf.teams: NwAy blue (triple melee, two mesmers) against SKT red (curses necromancer balance, ritualist in the 8 slot)
457b3a21-b67f-5164-a70d-adfd73423fcf.alignment: SKT AoB Derv death 3:45, NwAy Dervish and Prot deaths 6:53 and 7:13, NwAy knights 7:39 and 8:02, NwAy split takes SKT's archer and knight 8:30 to 8:52, SKT holds the stand 6:44 to 22:18, SKT wipes 20:34 to 21:31 and 23:12 to 24:05, NwAy Dervish takes the Bodyguard 27:02

claims.claim: SKT's ritualist in the 8 slot means five and a half damage and less backline healing; the necromancer defends the frontline and the ritualist can hold off the elementalist-free Lisa dervish.

check.evidence: A build read.

claims.claim: Korean guilds load in later, so they usually don't see the enemy build in time.

check.evidence: Load order isn't in the replay.

claims.claim: NwAy pushed in before its window: SKT just held the flag and waited, so NwAy fought early, under pressure, and lost the window.

check.evidence: SKT held its flag 2:38 to 4:41 before capping; the first death (SKT's AoB Derv, 3:45) went NwAy's way.

claims.claim: SKT's first death made NwAy's warrior the Boss (September's flux), the best character to hold it in the match.

check.evidence: SKT's AoB Derv died at 3:45.

claims.variable: who holds the Boss status (flux), and each transfer by a kill

claims.claim: NwAy wiped to get its flag in, so SKT's lack of a backup flag didn't matter; SKT then took both knights before the res.

check.evidence: NwAy lost Dervish (6:53) and Prot (7:13), then an archer (7:27) and knights at 7:39 and 8:02.

claims.claim: SKT's base defence was slow to react to NwAy's split, so it got free pit NPCs.

check.evidence: NwAy's split took SKT's outside archer (8:30), a knight (8:43) and an archer (8:52).

claims.claim: Defending the split with the necromancer is hard in the open: SKT took a death on the 7 monk before the collapse arrived.

check.evidence: SKT's 7 Monk died at 14:07 on the push side (5v5).

claims.claim: NwAy sneaking its Lisa dervish into the pit was very smart: SKT's split defenders couldn't follow, so it got an archer and was a fraction of a second from a second knight.

check.evidence: SKT lost an archer at 18:35 to NwAy's split.

claims.claim: SKT was picked apart without its necromancer at main and almost wiped; with its pit nearly empty by 22:00, only the Bodyguard was left.

check.evidence: SKT lost 6 players from 20:49 to 21:31, then archers at 21:45 and 21:52, a knight at 22:03 and an outside archer at 22:20.

claims.claim: SKT wiped pushing into NwAy's front with its prot and ritualist, and its ranger and warrior died just after time: catastrophic.

check.evidence: SKT lost 7 players from 23:27 to 24:05; the Ranger at 23:59 and the Hammer at 24:05 (after time).

claims.claim: SKT gaining full position for 26:00 forced NwAy to go the long way round through the portal; NwAy's Lisa then killed the Bodyguard but couldn't end it, and SKT won on Lord damage by a hair.

check.evidence: NwAy's Dervish took SKT's Bodyguard at 27:02 and died at 27:07; SKT won at 28:00 (NwAy lost its archers and Bodyguard at 28:02).

claims.claim: A key moment: SKT's mesmer cancelled the interrupt with a Pact to get the res off through NwAy's mesmer.

check.evidence: Cancels and Pact casts on the res aren't checked here.

8de08cc4-4baa-58dc-a6c9-fd22e4d4f04f.teams: cope blue (ranger spirit light weapon balance) against Book red (double elementalist split with Grenth's dervish and spirit light weapon)
8de08cc4-4baa-58dc-a6c9-fd22e4d4f04f.alignment: Book 7 Monk deaths 7:42, 12:37 and 17:49, cope Mesmer death 14:12, Book wipe 18:40 to 20:59, cope boosts 19:50, 21:50 and 23:50, Book wipe 23:54 to 25:19

claims.claim: cope has no snares and no enchantment removal on its split defence, so it will struggle to kill Book's split, which carries support skills (Spirit Bond, Healing Breeze) on every member.
claims.variable: collapse_snare

check.evidence: Book's splitters never died on split in the first 18 minutes; its deaths came at main.

claims.claim: With a 3-damage split you are liable to meet a stalling base defence, so it's on your main team to win, and for that you have to be ahead on flags.

check.evidence: Book's main lost its 7 Monk at 12:37 even though cope was the team behind then (cope capped at 12:55, 63 s after Book), and again at 17:49 (cope capped 23 s after Book): Book's main died whichever side was behind.

claims.claim: Book's 7 monk went down and made cope's dervish the Boss (September's flux).

check.evidence: Book's 7 Monk died at 7:42 at the stand.

claims.variable: who holds the Boss status (flux), and each transfer by a kill

claims.claim: Keeping the spirit light weapon on split while the two elementalists split apart weakens both sides: two elementalists together on split with the spirit light weapon at main would stabilize Book's main and free its 8 monk.
claims.variable: split_size

check.evidence: A configuration not played. Across 144 matches, 3-player and 4-player splits into the enemy base took a pit NPC equally often (36% against 35%, unclear; 122 splits).

claims.claim: Book took out cope's backline pressure only when cope fell behind on flags; behind on flags with a passive base defence is what a balance team can't afford.

check.evidence: cope's Mesmer died at 14:12 after Book had capped at 13:37; cope capped next at 15:08.

claims.claim: With three monks Book still lost its 7 monk to three of cope's damage.

check.evidence: Book's 7 Monk died at 17:49 on the backside (5v3).

claims.claim: Book's whole main team died and half its split, its mesmer was dead for a minute and a half with no res, and Book's monks became target practice.

check.evidence: Book lost 7 players from 18:55 to 20:59, and again from 21:35 to 23:11.

claims.claim: Spirit light weapon split builds make splits more dynamic (2, 3 or 4 damage splits); with all Book's support skills, cope found it very hard to kill on split when defending with two monks.

check.evidence: Book's split lost no one until the main collapsed; cope won by killing Book's main.

506102ee-ef94-5ecf-a485-c1c836193322.result: NwAy won at 28:00 on Lord damage
506102ee-ef94-5ecf-a485-c1c836193322.teams: NwAy blue (double elementalist split, spirit light weapon) against Men red (ranger spirit light weapon balance)
506102ee-ef94-5ecf-a485-c1c836193322.alignment: Men's outside archers 0:30 and 0:38, Men's ritualist captures throughout, Men Ranger death 8:19, NwAy wipe 9:10 to 10:01, NwAy's 3-player split takes Men's archer 14:13, Men Hammer death 16:45, Men knight 17:08, Men wipe 21:19 to 21:47 with knight 21:56 and archer 22:35, Men push and wipe 26:53 to 27:13

claims.claim: Weeping Stone is hard to collapse on, so a split there depends on winning its matchups more than on surviving collapses; the return tech matters less there than on Frozen.

check.evidence: A map read.

claims.claim: Having Shadow of Haste at main when the enemy doesn't keeps a team permanently ahead on flags.

check.evidence: Men's ritualist made most of Men's captures and answered within 4 to 31 s from 3:10 to 5:52 (NwAy's captures came 52 to 97 s after Men's).

claims.claim: With gate lock control, Men could reinforce the split defence through the gate and drag NwAy into an escalated fight, which is very bad for a split.

check.evidence: Gates aren't in the replay data (open item).

claims.claim: Men's ranger, pushed up on the ritualist too long, went down and made NwAy's air elementalist the Boss (September's flux).

check.evidence: Men's Ranger died at 8:19 on the push side (3v4).

claims.variable: who holds the Boss status (flux), and each transfer by a kill

claims.claim: Losing face and giving up gate control is a split's great weakness on Weeping Stone: Men's warrior power played and killed NwAy's 7 and 6 monks, and the mesmer died after time with no res.

check.evidence: NwAy's 7 Monk and Prot died at the stand at 9:25 and 9:28; NwAy's Mesmer died at 10:01 (after time).

claims.claim: NwAy's air elementalist sneaking an archer is huge: in a game going to 28:00, pit NPCs decide it.

check.evidence: Men lost an archer at 14:13 to NwAy's split with no defender present.

claims.claim: Men's warrior disconnected and was caught and killed with a minute to the base res.

check.evidence: Men's Hammer died at 16:45 on the backside.

claims.claim: NwAy's 3-player split (ritualist back at main) is much better for it than the 4-player one: a 3v3 is bad for a team defending with two monks, and keeping the spirit light weapon at main protects NwAy's 7 monk.
claims.variable: split_size

check.evidence: NwAy's 4-player splits (ritualist with them, to 2:53) took nothing; its 3-player splits from 12:53 took an archer (14:13), a knight (17:08), an outside archer (17:32), a knight (21:56), an archer (22:35) and the Bodyguard (28:02). In general (144 matches) 3-player and 4-player splits took a pit NPC equally often (36% against 35%, unclear), so it held in this match, not yet as a rule.

claims.claim: Men's base was left with only the Bodyguard and NwAy's elementalists farmed Lord damage; without its pit NPCs Men had to try to end the game and couldn't.

check.evidence: Men's push at 26:53 took a knight but Men lost three players by 27:13; NwAy won on Lord damage.

claims.claim: Men's hold to the last second gave it a player advantage and a boost at the critical 27:00 timing, but not enough to overcome the Lord damage already farmed.

check.evidence: Men boosted at 27:04.

b31ffe18-07a9-589f-a516-8862f80ab668.teams: xxx blue (mobile WoC spike with Return and dashes) against Men red (ranger spirit light weapon balance)
b31ffe18-07a9-589f-a516-8862f80ab668.alignment: Men's split from 0:10, Men Mesmer death 0:55, Men Ranger death 1:22, Men 7 Monk death 2:36, Men knight 2:49, Men Ranger death 3:32, Men knight 4:32, first 8v8 7:10, Men wipes 7:23 to 8:18

claims.claim: A mobile WoC spike opens the 8v8 with immediate kills but crumbles in a long engagement, since its bars are spent on smiting and mobility, not party-wide stability.

check.evidence: xxx killed early (0:55, 1:22, 2:36) and won the only long 8v8 too (7:10 to 8:18).

claims.claim: Men lost its mesmer in its own base engaging a 2v3 defence: a big mistake.

check.evidence: Men's Mesmer died at 0:55 on the backside (3v6).

claims.claim: xxx's Return onto its own archers makes splitting dangerous: Men should kill those outside archers to limit the mobility.

check.evidence: Men's ranger died at 1:22 and Men killed xxx's outside archer only at 2:58.

claims.claim: xxx committed into Men's base and took out the 7 monk at once; Flesh would have been better than Death Pact for Men here.

check.evidence: Men's 7 Monk died at 2:36 in its own base; Men lost a knight at 2:49.

claims.claim: Men's ranger stuck in the enemy base went down with 30 death penalty.

check.evidence: Men's Ranger died at 3:32 on the push side (3v6), its third death.

claims.claim: xxx's snares and the NPCs blocking kept Men committed in the base; Blessed Light alone can't clear that many snares.

check.evidence: Men lost an archer (4:08) and a knight (4:32) while fighting in its own base.

claims.claim: In the first 8v8, xxx killed immediately (45 death penalty on the ranger), then caught Men's 8 monk but lost its warrior doing it.

check.evidence: At 7:10 Men's Hammer died and xxx's 8 Monk died; Men's Ranger had died at 6:38.

claims.claim: Men pushed too deep into xxx's base with a lot of death penalty; it could have pulled back and held for a boost. With both Pacts down after time, Men resigned.

check.evidence: Men lost 7 players from 7:23 to 8:18 in xxx's pit and push side; the match ended at about 8:34.

claims.claim: The mobile WoC spike can be beaten 8v8 by a balanced build with the right 8 bars and mesmer bar, if it doesn't give up death penalty first.

check.evidence: One match; Men lost this one.

b5760ac4-e21a-54d0-a6ea-d6b5bb0d0e5d.result: Men won at 13:57 by killing the Guild Lord, 2 s before a base res
b5760ac4-e21a-54d0-a6ea-d6b5bb0d0e5d.teams: Men (hammer, dervish, ranger, mesmer, spirit light weapon ritualist, three monks) against NwAy (hammer, two Avatar of Lyssa dervishes, two mesmers, three monks)
b5760ac4-e21a-54d0-a6ea-d6b5bb0d0e5d.alignment: NwAy's first cap 0:15 and Men's overcap 0:18, NwAy falls back 1:26, NwAy's four man split from 1:46, its 8 Monk dies 3:36 and 5:22, Mes/A dies 3:58 (based), five man split fight 7:06, knight 9:41, back cap 9:46, Mes/A based at 10:00 and Hammer dead just after it (resurrected 10:05), Men's Mesmer and 7 Monk 10:42, Men's dervish dies carrying 11:15, NwAy's 8 Monk 12:09, Lord 13:57

claims.claim: NwAy has no party-wide protection against a ranger balance and one party heal, so it can't stand in the 8v8: it has to fall back at once and split.
claims.variable: party-wide defence against ranged pressure, as a build feature that decides whether to stand or split

check.evidence: NwAy fell back from the stand to its front door at 1:26 with team health at 67% and split four from 1:46.

claims.claim: Men's single runner with a run skill keeps flags going alone; NwAy has to send a second player back each time, so in a straight 8v8 Men is often a player up.
claims.variable: seconds each runner is away from the fight per flag

check.evidence: 8 v 7 for Men from 0:44 to 1:20 while NwAy's Hammer was away (he returned 36 s behind); Men's own runner also cost a player from 1:20.

claims.claim: NwAy's four man split (two dervishes, Mes/A, 8 Monk) is met by Men's hammer, ranger and two monks.

check.evidence: Men's 8 Monk went back at 1:39, Hammer, Ranger and Prot at 1:55; 4 v 4 at Men's back door from 2:42.

claims.claim: NwAy's 8 Monk dies on the split because he is pushed into the range of two archers and crippled, with no shadow step to get out; a split monk without one can't escape.
claims.variable: NPC damage and snares on a split's monk; whether the split's monk has an escape

check.evidence: He died at 3:36 in Men's base and again at 5:22; archer damage and snares on him aren't measured in the story.

claims.claim: NwAy's Mes/A dies just before the base res, so the death costs little time.

check.evidence: Died 3:58, based at 4:00.

claims.claim: At main, NwAy's four can only win if it gets ahead on flags; its window is the short time Men's runner is away, and it has to kill the footmen first to reach the 7 Monk.
claims.variable: the window while the enemy's runner is away; footmen alive as cover for a monk

check.evidence: The story shows who is away and when, but not footmen as cover for a monk standing in them.

claims.claim: One dervish coming home forces Men's four out of NwAy's base and saves the knights; when he leaves to rejoin the split Men push back in, and he comes home again.
claims.variable: one returning defender turning a base fight

check.evidence: He went back at 7:17 and Men were pushed out at 7:24; Men pushed in again at 7:54; he was back at 8:00 and Men out at 8:02. The story has each move but doesn't link them.

claims.claim: With both halves even and stalled, the only way for NwAy to move the game on is to take a flag out; it does so late.

check.evidence: NwAy capped nothing from 5:00 until its dervish's back cap at 9:46 (flag picked up 8:56).

claims.claim: NwAy's Mes/A dies on the split just before the base res and comes back in his own base, putting NwAy a player up there; its hammer dies just after the res and needs a skill res. NwAy then kills Men's mesmer and 7 Monk.
claims.variable: base res as a change of numbers where the dead player was needed

check.evidence: Mes/A died 9:58 and was based; Hammer died 9:59 and was not (resurrected 10:05); 4 v 5 at NwAy's front door from 10:14; Men's Mesmer and 7 Monk died 10:42. The story's clock had the Hammer 0 s before the res; it now reads whether the res took him.

claims.claim: Men's dervish tries to give his life for a cap to deny NwAy's boost, worth trying because NwAy carries death penalty; he falls short.

check.evidence: He picked the flag up at 10:56 and died holding it at the stand at 11:15; NwAy boosted at 11:46.

claims.claim: After the boost NwAy pushes all eight into Men's base and is caught in a bad spot as Men's dead come back; its 8 Monk dies right after the base res, the rest are routed and Men has time to kill the Lord before the next one.
claims.variable: pushing into a base shortly before the defenders' base res

check.evidence: 5 v 8 at Men's pit at 11:48, base res 12:00, NwAy's 8 Monk died 12:09 (111 s before the next res), 8 v 7 at 12:10, all eight dead by 13:30, Lord 13:57.

2615ca0c-12b4-5ae6-a73d-53c0f0fc627c.result: yM won at 15:07 by killing the Guild Lord
2615ca0c-12b4-5ae6-a73d-53c0f0fc627c.teams: Rudi (primal rage warrior, dervish, two mesmers, smiting monk with Word of Censure, three monks) against yM (hammer, sword warrior, mesmer, curses necromancer, spirit light weapon ritualist, three monks)
2615ca0c-12b4-5ae6-a73d-53c0f0fc627c.alignment: yM's Ritualist dies in Rudi's pit 1:10, Rudi's flag returned 3:17, Rudi's overcap 3:49, Rudi's split away 3:56 to 5:26, Rudi's Stand Mes dies 6:36, yM's cap 7:00, Rudi's knight 8:22, yM's Prot dies 9:22 (resurrected 9:33), Rudi's smiting monk dies carrying 10:38, Rudi's deaths 11:00 to 11:44, Rudi's Warrior dies at yM's front footies 14:30, Lord 15:07

claims.claim: yM opens with its ritualist alone at Rudi's back door; Rudi has nobody suited to defend him and few snares. Because yM brings no second flag, it looks to Rudi as if the ritualist is only waiting back for one.
claims.variable: the opening split: players who never join the main team

check.evidence: Only seven yM at the stand from 0:12; Rudi's Mes/A left at 0:38 and Warrior at 0:50. The story doesn't narrate a split that starts at 0:00.

claims.claim: The ritualist nearly kills a knight, then runs back into the returning warrior and dies; under September's flux that hands the Boss status to Rudi's mesmer, who can then defend him alone. A large mistake: a split player has to watch for the collapse.
claims.variable: who holds the Boss status (flux), and each transfer by a kill

check.evidence: yM's Ritualist died in Rudi's pit at 1:10. Who holds the Boss status isn't in the data.

claims.claim: Rudi's flag is returned, the commentator can't see how.

check.evidence: Rudi's Warrior dropped it at 3:01 and yM's 7 Monk returned it at 3:17: the story adds who.

claims.claim: Rudi splits its warrior and a mesmer although the 8v8 should suit it; the split needs a monk to do anything. When it rejoins main ahead of yM's defenders Rudi is briefly a player or two up, but is under pressure and can't use it.
claims.variable: arriving ahead of the defenders after a split collapses, and whether the lead was used

check.evidence: Split away 3:56 to 5:26; 8 v 6 at the stand at 5:26, 8 v 8 at 5:42 (yM 12 s behind); no kill.

claims.claim: Rudi gives up the 8v8 to run a flag on its warrior, and loses a mesmer left too far forward as it pulls back.

check.evidence: Warrior left for the flag at 6:18; Stand Mes died at the stand at 6:36.

claims.claim: Rudi splits again without taking a flag out the back (it is left at the front), so there is no back cap; the split does nothing and lets yM bring another flag.

check.evidence: Flag dropped at Rudi's front door 6:55; split from 7:33, met by yM's Ritualist and 8 Monk; yM's main took a knight at 8:22.

claims.claim: Rudi runs its flag in on the smiting monk too boldly: he dies, and three Rudi monks follow.

check.evidence: He died holding the flag at the stand at 10:38; Prot died 11:00, 7 Monk and two more 11:12.

claims.claim: yM's ritualist detours to kill the outside archers before rejoining, so Rudi is a player up for a while; if Rudi can't win 8 v 7 it won't win 8 v 8.

check.evidence: 8 v 7 in Rudi's pit from 12:40, 8 v 8 at 13:10 (yM 30 s behind); Rudi lost six players from 13:36 to 13:58.

claims.claim: Rudi's warrior leaves the base without a flag, is chased into yM's archer and footmen and dies there.

check.evidence: 1 v 1 at yM's front footies at 14:20; he died there at 14:30.

5f380eb5-7b0f-5b35-acbd-b82c08e02750.result: xxx won at 7:35 by killing the Guild Lord
5f380eb5-7b0f-5b35-acbd-b82c08e02750.teams: cope (hex build with five casters, air elementalist, spirit light weapon ritualist) against xxx (six necromancers building a minion army, two monks)

claims.variable: the opening split: players who never join the main team

check.evidence: The story first says xxx's three 'go to split' at 2:00; a split from 0:00 isn't narrated.

claims.claim: NwAy answers with a passive three man base defence whose hammer runs flags, and plays a player up at main. With continuous double running it stalls the split and builds a kill threat at main; a split on Corrupted Isle is hard against that.
claims.variable: passive base defence with a player up at main; share of flags double run

check.evidence: Both teams double ran to 5:14; NwAy lost no pit NPC until 11:24; xxx's main fell back under pressure at 2:14 and 7:12.

claims.claim: Each time the hammer comes home with a flag he forces the split out before it can build pressure; the split's monk can't follow him out.
claims.variable: one returning defender turning a base fight

check.evidence: Same link as in Men v NwAy 2: the story has the moves but doesn't tie a defender's return to the split leaving.

claims.claim: With its 8 Monk on the split, xxx's main is crushed: it drops the flag, gives up footmen, then knights and front NPCs, while the split runs out of energy having killed nothing. The gamble fails.

check.evidence: xxx lost a knight at 6:49, fell back into its base at 7:12 (team health 81%) and NwAy boosted at 7:14; NwAy held the stand to the end.

claims.claim: xxx's main pushes too far forward while short of players and is caught; both monks die a minute before the base res. NwAy then turns on the collapsing split, and the ritualist, with no shadow step, is left to die.

check.evidence: 7 Monk died 8:56 (64 s before the res), Prot 9:06 (54 s), Ritualist 9:31.

claims.claim: xxx's air elementalist dies just before the base res; the fire elementalist just after it, by a fraction of a second.

check.evidence: Air Ele died 11:40 and was based at 12:00; Fire Ele died 11:58 and was not. The replay clock puts him 2 s before the res, so the story now reads the outcome instead of the clock.

claims.claim: The air elementalist runs to NwAy's base and takes one knight, sending NwAy home.

check.evidence: The story has two NwAy knights lost, at 11:24 and 11:35; the commentator saw one.

claims.claim: Far behind, xxx can't push a base without its flag capped; it would do better to keep a flag in hand while the elementalists run the defenders around.

check.evidence: NwAy held the stand from 5:14 to the end and boosted every two minutes from 7:14.
